c.tagline: The Garden City and beating heart of the Ashanti kingdom, ringed by kente and gold.

taxi.fareNote: Shared 'dropping' taxis are unmetered — agree the price before setting off. App rides (Uber, Bolt, Yango) are widely available, usually cheaper than street taxis and avoid haggling.

emergency.note: 112 works as a general emergency line from mobile phones; 192 reaches the fire service. Response can be slow, so many visitors go directly to a private hospital.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in the dense crowds of Kejetia Market and Adum, especially with phones out.

hood_desc: The dense central business district and main shopping core, packed with stores, banks, forex bureaux and street stalls; the convenient, if hectic, walkable heart of the city for first-timers.
The royal and cultural quarter around the Manhyia Palace and its museum, seat of the Asantehene and the living heart of Ashanti tradition; best for history and the Akwasidae festival.

An upscale, leafy residential area south-west of the centre with many of Kumasi's better hotels, restaurants and bars; suits travellers wanting comfortable dining and nightlife within reach of the centre.
The area around Kejetia and the Central Market, one of the largest open-air markets in West Africa — a sprawling maze of kente, crafts, food and goods; a paradise for shoppers and people-watchers.
A quieter, more spacious residential and commercial district in the south with a shopping mall, offices and mid-range hotels; good for a calmer base with modern conveniences.

water.note: Drink bottled or sealed sachet water; avoid tap.

transit.hours: Tro-tros and shared taxis run from early morning until mid-evening; after dark, app rides and taxis fill the gap.
transit.note: Kumasi has no metro or tram and no regular passenger rail. The city moves by tro-tro (shared minibus), shared and 'dropping' taxis, and ride-hailing apps.
transit.pay: Tro-tro and taxi fares are paid in cash (Ghanaian Cedi) to the driver or mate; there is no transit card. Mobile-money is common for app rides and many shops.

bus: Intercity coaches to Accra and beyond (STC, VIP, VVIP, OA Travel & Tours)
train: No regular passenger rail service (the Kumasi-Accra line is not in scheduled operation)

transit.m: Airport taxi to Adum / city centre (~20 min)

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up the bill or leaving small change for good service is appreciated but not required.
